title: Triad construction
description: Memorize the four qualities, letter spelling, and the strings 4–3–2 fret recipes.

cards.front: What is a triad?
cards.back: Three pitch classes stacked in thirds: a root, a third above it, and a fifth above that.

cards.front: Name the four common triad qualities.
cards.back: Major, minor, diminished, and augmented.

cards.front: Give the stack, formula, half steps from the root, and symbols for a major triad.
cards.back: M3 + m3. Formula 1 3 5. Half steps 0 4 7. Written C or Cmaj.

cards.front: Give the stack, formula, half steps from the root, and symbols for a minor triad.
cards.back: m3 + M3. Formula 1 ♭3 5. Half steps 0 3 7. Written Cm or Cmin.

cards.front: Give the stack, formula, half steps from the root, and symbols for a diminished triad.
cards.back: m3 + m3. Formula 1 ♭3 ♭5. Half steps 0 3 6. Written Cdim or C°.

cards.front: Give the stack, formula, half steps from the root, and symbols for an augmented triad.
cards.back: M3 + M3. Formula 1 3 ♯5. Half steps 0 4 8. Written Caug or C+.

cards.front: What does the third decide? What does the fifth decide?
cards.back: The third separates major from minor. The fifth is perfect in major and minor, lowered in diminished, and raised in augmented.

cards.front: Which letters does a C triad use, and why?
cards.back: C E G. A triad uses three letters a third apart: the root, two letters up, four letters up. Accidentals change the sound; they do not change the letters.

cards.front: What two methods should agree when you build any triad?
cards.back: From the major scale on the root: take 1 3 5 and alter. From stacked thirds: a major third is 4 half steps, a minor third is 3.

cards.front: What is the three-step spelling procedure?
cards.back: Write the three letters (root, +2, +4). Apply the formula to set accidentals. Check the half-step counts: 0 4 7, 0 3 7, 0 3 6, or 0 4 8.

cards.front: C E♭ G is C minor. Why is C D♯ G not a spelling of C minor?
cards.back: It can sound the same on guitar, but D is not a third above C. Do not trade correct letters for easier accidentals.

cards.front: Spell E augmented, F♯ diminished, and D♭ major.
cards.back: E G♯ B♯ (fifth takes B, not C). F♯ A C (perfect fifth is C♯, so diminished fifth is C). D♭ F A♭ (F is natural).

cards.front: Why can one augmented triad have three possible roots?
cards.back: Two stacked major thirds divide the octave into three equal parts. C E G♯ is also E G♯ B♯ (E augmented) and A♭ C E (A♭ augmented). The spelling tells you which root is meant. Diminished triads are not symmetric.

cards.front: What typical jobs do major, minor, diminished, and augmented triads have?
cards.back: Major is stable and bright (I, IV, V in major). Minor is stable and darker (i in minor; ii, iii, vi in major). Diminished is unstable (vii° in major, ii° in minor). Augmented is rare and usually passing.

cards.front: What pitch classes are doubled in open C (x32010), Am (x02210), and G (320003)?
cards.back: C is C E G C E on strings 5–1. Am is A E A C E. G is G B D G B G on strings 6–1. These are voicings of one triad, not different chords.

cards.front: On strings 4–3–2 with root G at fret 5, give frets and notes for all four qualities.
cards.back: Major 5 4 3 (G B D). Minor 5 3 3 (G B♭ D). Diminished 5 3 2 (G B♭ D♭). Augmented 5 4 4 (G B D♯).

cards.front: On strings 4–3–2, how do you change quality by moving one note?
cards.back: Major to minor: third down one fret. Minor to diminished: fifth down one fret. Major to augmented: fifth up one fret.

cards.front: With root C on string 4 fret 10, give the four fret recipes on strings 4–3–2.
cards.back: Major 10 9 8, minor 10 8 8, diminished 10 8 7, augmented 10 9 9.

cards.front: Why does the major shape on strings 4–3–2 descend (5 4 3 for G)?
cards.back: String 4 to 3 is a 5-half-step gap and a major third is 4, so the third sits one fret lower. String 4 to 2 is a 9-half-step gap and a perfect fifth is 7, so the fifth sits two frets lower.

cards.front: Spell major triads on D, F, A, B♭, E♭, and F♯.
cards.back: D F♯ A; F A C; A C♯ E; B♭ D F; E♭ G B♭; F♯ A♯ C♯.

cards.front: Spell minor triads on E, A, B, C, F♯, and B♭.
cards.back: E G B; A C E; B D F♯; C E♭ G; F♯ A C♯; B♭ D♭ F.

cards.front: Spell diminished triads on B, F♯, C, G, and A.
cards.back: B D F; F♯ A C; C E♭ G♭; G B♭ D♭; A C E♭.

cards.front: Spell augmented triads on C, D, E, and F.
cards.back: C E G♯; D F♯ A♯; E G♯ B♯; F A C♯.

cards.front: Name the root and quality: A C♯ E; D F A♭; E♭ G♭ B♭; G B♭ D♭; B D♯ F♯.
cards.back: A major, D diminished, E♭ minor, G diminished, B major.

cards.front: Find the error: G B D♯ called G major; C E♭ G♭ called C minor; E G♯ C called E augmented.
cards.back: G B D♯ is G augmented. C E♭ G♭ is C diminished. E G♯ C should be spelled E G♯ B♯.

cards.front: On strings 4–3–2 with root D at fret 12, give all four qualities with notes.
cards.back: Major 12 11 10 (D F♯ A). Minor 12 10 10 (D F A). Diminished 12 10 9 (D F A♭). Augmented 12 11 11 (D F♯ A♯).
